Join us as a Senior Business Analyst and help transform government processes into smarter, more efficient services for the Cayman Islands. Cayman Islands Government Computer Services Department Senior Business Analyst (SBA) Salary Range: CI$77,088 - $101,160 per annum (US $92,506 – $121,392) The primary role of the Senior Business Analyst (SBA ) is to ensure that business processes and supporting systems continue to meet business project stakeholder needs and government’s strategic directions and objectives. The role of the SBA is to lead and facilitate business process improvement/reengineering/ (BPI/R) for projects across Government to: improve customer experience and efficiency, to enhance or create competitive advantage for the Cayman Islands and to reduce cost to provide services. This position deals with the more tactical, day-to-day aspects of discovering, validating, documenting and communicating business-process-related knowledge through modelling, simulating and analysing current and future states. Qualifications The post requires: Minimum of a Bachelor's degree or equivalent in science, engineering or business, with at least seven (7) years of related business discipline experience. An M.B.A. or other advanced degree in business or social sciences with at least five (5) years of related business discipline experience would be preferred; OR A more mature entrant with an industry-recognized relevant technical accreditation plus a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant post-accreditation experience. Additional qualifications/certifications in Business Process Modelling and Notation (BPMN) and Business Process Improvements (BPI) and programme and project management would be a distinct advantage. Experience The post requires: Three (3) years of process improvement experience, especially experience that leverages technology as part of the solution. Hands-on experience with process modelling, analysis and simulation tools. Experience working on projects using a variety of process redesign methods (such as Lean Six Sigma, Kaizen, Total Quality Management etc.). Track record of working on projects that delivered different types of business outcomes: revenue growth and customer satisfaction, for example, not just process efficiency or cost reduction. Experience with the full Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), including the end-to-end test cycle, as well as agile/iterative development and delivery. Business domain experience in the process areas being supported would be advantageous. Broad experience and working knowledge of Government’s organisational structure and functions, including budget and financial control and personnel management procedures will be beneficial. Skills: The post requires: Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication, including excellent presentation and interviewing skills. Ability to work within high-performing virtual teams and highly collaborative. Command of the BPM modelling notation (such as Business Process Model and Notation [BPMN]) used by the organization. Knowledge and experience in business process modelling and analysis tools. Knowledge and experience in BPI methods, such as Lean Six Sigma, as well as more modern, agile methods. Background in root cause, bottleneck, impact and other process (not systems) analysis methods. Data gathering, and quantitative and qualitative data analysis, including business process metrics and measures linking to business KPIs. Able to change process models and rules in BPMS or other BPM technologies. Knowledge of finance, accounting, valuation and metrics development; statistical analysis skills are a plus. Teaching/educating/coaching/mentoring stakeholders toward desired business outcomes. Good knowledge of various computer-based tools such as Microsoft Office, JIRA and project management software such as Teamwork/ Microsoft Project. Familiarity with application delivery methods, experience with e-commerce, Web architecture, and Internet/intranet development and implementation is a plus. Project management and change management skills and experience is a plus. The post includes excellent benefits as determined by the Public Service Management Act and Regulations (2018 Revision), the Public Service Pensions Law (2023 Revision) and the CINICO Health Plan. This currently includes 25 days paid vacation, 11 public holidays, 12% employer paid pension and comprehensive health insurance. The post offers full relocation support for the employee and dependents.
